source.title: Sub-Billion, Super-Frontier: Small Language Models Rival Zero-Shot Frontier LLMs on General and Literary Relation Extraction

record.tranche_reason: Tests downstream RE performance across model sizes using positive-class micro-F1 rather than held-out pretraining loss; it does not reproduce the original loss-scaling measurement.
record.gate_note: The paper cites language-model scaling laws but does not measure held-out cross-entropy loss, training tokens, training compute, or compute-optimal allocation. Its own relevant result is a within-family parameter-scale comparison of downstream RE F1. Results on prompt format, domain adaptation, and frontier comparisons are not rows for the scaling claim.
record.test_reason: In a new setting (QLoRA task-tuned relation extraction), the paper reports within-family size contrasts of downstream positive-class micro-F1 (Table 5). These bear weakly on V6, whether downstream performance improves with scale. With only two sizes per family, predictability cannot be assessed, and no loss, token or compute measures exist for V1–V5 or V7. T3 rather than T2: this is a new downstream setting with a result on the claim, not a different method aimed at the loss law.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors find the clean same-generation Qwen2.5 scale gain marginal (+0.037, flat on GenTune) and the SmolLM gain confounded with a generation change. They explicitly decline to read scale effects as a scaling law. Their broader conclusion is that task adaptation and data composition, not raw scale, drive RE performance; sub-billion tuned models match 3B models and beat zero-shot frontier LLMs.
record.recipe_differences: Compares QLoRA fine-tuned model sizes on downstream relation-extraction F1, not pretrained models on held-out cross-entropy loss; no token or compute sweep.
record.method_sensitivity: Results differ by model family and tuning regime; the SmolLM size contrast also crosses a model generation. The analysis excludes two anomalous 0-shot configurations.
record.problems: Only two within-family scale contrasts are available; SmolLM2-360M to SmolLM3-3B changes generation as well as size. The models are fine-tuned for the task, results are single-seed, and this study does not measure pretraining loss or training compute.

untested.parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or compute; not measured.
Extrapolation of fitted laws; no fits on loss.
Other modalities or training regimes. The fine-tuning setting has only two size points per family and no power-law fit.
Predictability (a fitted trend or extrapolation) across many scales, and prediction from pretraining loss. Only two sizes per family and one task family (relation extraction after QLoRA fine-tuning).
Dependence of exponents or the compute-optimal split on fitting choices; curve bending.

missing.what: RoBERTa encoder baseline 125M→355M (within-family scale-up): General Avg falls from 0.826 to 0.814. The authors attribute this to single-seed instability on NYT11/Re-DocRED and call it a general-domain scaling probe.

Regression of micro-F1 on log10(params): slope +0.129 per 10× [+0.077,+0.196]; with family fixed effects +0.114 [+0.065,+0.180]. The authors say it is driven largely by the confounded SmolLM contrast.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'supports' label rested largely on the SmolLM rows, which are generation-confounded; I removed it and set those rows to cannot_determine. Section 4.2's interaction paragraph says 'scale provides a consistent advantage', which is inconsistent with the authors' own Table 5 reading; the verdict follows Table 5. The frontier-vs-SLM comparisons (undisclosed sizes, zero-shot vs fine-tuned) are not scale tests. All runs are single-seed; the CIs cover test sampling only. V6 bearing is weak: only two size points per family, and the models are off-the-shelf releases, not a controlled pretraining sweep.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute.
Whether power laws fitted on small runs predict loss on much larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocations and their trends with compute.
Controlled architecture comparisons at fixed parameter count.
Power-law behavior in other modalities or training regimes.

Tests downstream performance only on relation-extraction benchmarks and only through two within-family size contrasts; does not test predictability from pretraining loss or across a broad range of scales and tasks.
Does not test dependence of loss-law exponents or compute-optimal allocations on fitting choices, nor whether pretraining-loss curves bend away from a power law.

relationships.condition: Same-generation Qwen2.5 0.5B→3B, QLoRA task-tuned RE, LitTune/MixTune/overall
relationships.reason: A 6× parameter increase yields only +0.034 to +0.053 F1 (overall +0.037), a weak downstream scale effect after task fine-tuning (r2, r3, r4).
relationships.display_finding: F1 increased by only 0.034–0.053, with an overall gain of 0.037.

relationships.reason: General-domain F1 does not improve with 6× scale (−0.004), i.e. no downstream scale gain (r1).
relationships.display_finding: Increasing model size sixfold from 0.5B to 3B decreased general-domain F1 by 0.004.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Positive scale-associated effects in the tested within-family comparisons
reader_labels.reason: F1 rises in the reported Qwen2.5 LitTune and MixTune contrasts and in all three SmolLM regime contrasts, although the SmolLM comparison also changes generation (r2, r3, r5, r6, r7).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: The two within-family comparisons and their tested regimes
reader_labels.reason: Effects are heterogeneous: the cleaner Qwen2.5 comparison is small overall and has no GenTune gain, while the larger SmolLM contrast is confounded with a generation change; the paper cautions against treating these data as a continuous scaling law (r1, r4, r8).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.reason: The larger Qwen2.5 model does not improve general-domain GenTune F1 in this comparison (r1).
